summary: Frontend-only, read-only testing of long-video support, slow-motion viewer, normal-speed/original video playback, bowling long-clip report, upload/pricing copy and regression. Nearly everything works. One copy problem: the pricing plan cards still say '30 seconds' / '30s each', which contradicts the new 'any length' line.

issues: Batting card description reads 'One video up to 30 seconds per batting analysis.' and Bowling card reads 'Up to three angles (30s each) per bowling analysis.' This contradicts the '... per analysis, any length' bullet on the same cards. Source: plan description strings in /app/backend/billing_routes.py lines 16 and 18 (PLAN_DEFAULTS seed). Existing plan docs in MongoDB probably need updating too, because the descriptions are served from the DB.

'Film 5–30 seconds...' and FAQ '5–30 second clips...' are still there. This is fine as filming advice, but it could make users think there is a limit. Consider rewording it, e.g. 'any length; we find the main shot'.

action_items: Update the Batting/Bowling plan descriptions in billing_routes.py PLAN_DEFAULTS and in the existing MongoDB plan documents to remove '30 seconds' / '30s each'
Optional: reword the landing page 'Film 5–30 seconds' step and the FAQ so they read as advice, not a limit
Optional: max_duration_s is still in the admin plan editor (Admin.jsx shows '30s' in the plan table) even though duration isn't enforced any more. Hide it or relabel it to avoid confusing admins
critical_code_review_comments: The viewer and the report-video use the same playback asset (130697...). The original-video-link points to a different asset (ffae40...). Both return 206 video/mp4. This is the intended behaviour.
AnalysisViewer speed testids come from r*100; 0.1*100 === 10 in JS, so 'viewer-speed-10' works, but this relies on floating-point luck. Hardcoded testids would be safer.
